diaryEntries.entry: May 21st 1918, I left Sandwich for Southampton at 8.20 AM.
I arrived at Southampton at 3 PM and left Southampton at 8 PM on board the Antrim for France.

I arrived at Le Harve at 3.30 AM on May 22nd. We walked about four miles to a Rest Camp where we had our dinner or 'at least' it was called a dinner. We had some white bread the first for years and it was lovely. I just managed to get a couple of bottles of beer which went down very good indeed.
We left Le Harve at 4 PM by train for Marseilles Passing through a very pretty part of France and was stopped on the way at midnight on May 22nd by an air Raid on Paris.
We had some biscuits and bully beef about 11 AM, the first food for 22 hours in fact all the time we were in the train we were fed once a day.
We arrived at Marseilles at midnight on Friday May 24th and slept in the train for the rest of the night.
Another Biscuit for Breakfast and fall in to march to the rest camp. About 2 miles we Reached the rest camp in the morning of May 25th very tired and thirsty.
Sunday May 26th me and my chum went for a walk by the sea front had 2 bottles of wine at 1/8 per large bottle, very good.
Monday May 27th cleaned up our camp and went for a walk along the sea front again. Very pretty place and very nice wine.

Tuesday May 28th we had a day in Marseilles and had a good time. It is a very pretty city very fine buildings and very nice wine. Wine is very cheap here, but beer is 1 and 10 per pint bottle but very good. I met some boys from off a ship all from Southampton and had a lively hour with them, but we had to be back in camp by 8.30 PM which we were and quite sober after having a splendid time.
Wednesday May 29th had a nice quiet day in Camp and had sports and racing in the evening
Thursday May 30th nobody allowed to leave the Camp special parade at 6.50PM 14 men were absent so nobody allowed to leave the Camp next day.

Friday May 31st had a splendid boxing competition in the evening and saw some good fighting by the black men. Nobody to leave the camp, under orders to pack up our bit to go away. Special parade at 5PM told we are leaving Rest Camp next day at 12.45 PM.

June 1st up very early in the morning rolled our blankets ready for return to the stores. Left rest camp for docks at 12.50 PM. Put on Board SS Ormonde for work in the docks as there is a dockers strike on here.
Sunday June 2nd told off for work as a steward to start work at 1.30PM had the morning off
Monday June 3rd start work at 7AM until midday, afternoon off, evening in Marseilles. Had a good time
Tuesday June 4th started work at 8AM finished at 11AM took our bit ashore in the afternoon.

Left the SS Ormonde at 6.30PM went on board the SS Indarra at 7.30PM. Very rough sleeping quarters, we slept on the floors and tables and on deck in fact anywhere. 32 men told off for table with room only for 16 men for meals. We have our meals in two sitting 16 each. Some hope we shall soon leave this ship we seem in for a rough time.
Breakfast 7.30AM everybody complaining.
A lot of French troops come aboard this afternoon. Parade at 2PM with lifebelts for boat drill and inspection.

June 5th left Marseilles at 4 PM, anchored just outside the harbour. For night I slept on deck under the stars and on the Mediterranean Sea on a lovely June night. A lot of fighting amongst the crew 2 fight on shore and 2 on board a very good start. One of the crews running about the deck with a damn great knife looking for trouble

Thursday June 6th laid outside the harbour all day. Had boat drill and told off to our boat stations and left Marseilles for good or see. At 11.15 PM escorted by eight Japanese Destroyers we have five big troop ship in our convoy.
